A.taste_why: The palette holds together: #232930 background, #a7b1bc foreground and a #6e9e9b teal accent give a soft, low-contrast dark theme. The ANSI colours are dusty and muted. The wallpaper is calm and easy to live with: a fogged horizon, hazy hills, a small lighthouse whose teal reflection is the only accent, and a dark jetty. The faint mirrored jetty posts above the deck read a little oddly. Yaru-sage leans green rather than teal.
A.implementation_why: colors.toml is complete and valid, with every key Omarchy's templates read. make-background.sh is tidy, strict-mode ImageMagick with a temp dir cleaned up on a trap. It is extra machinery shipped inside the theme folder, though harmless. There is no hyprland.lua, so borders fall back to template defaults, which is fine.
A.execution_why: It covers every part of the brief: the name, a cool grey-blue low-contrast palette, a muted teal accent, and a background image in backgrounds/1-harbour-fog.jpg.

B.taste_why: The palette is well judged; cyan equals the accent and the accent colours are desaturated. The teal-to-blue gradient border in hyprland.lua is tasteful. The wallpaper is the weak point: heavy smeared streaks cover both sky and water and make it look blurry and muddy. The lighthouse sits on a thin plank, and the rust-tinted railing in the corner feels awkward.
B.implementation_why: colors.toml is valid and complete. hyprland.lua uses proper rgba() values and gradient syntax for both general and group borders. Yaru-prussiangreen is a sensible teal-ish icon theme.
B.execution_why: It meets every part of the request, but the background reads more like stormy murk than calm harbour fog.

C.taste_why: This is the most evocative wallpaper: a misty harbour with a pier, two teal lamps reflected in the water, a sailboat, distant cranes, a veiled moon, and one tiny warm window. It is slightly busy, but the fog keeps it quiet. The palette is a touch darker (#1f252c) with #b3bdc7 text, still low contrast and coherent. Yaru-prussiangreen-dark suits the teal accent.
C.implementation_why: A minimal, clean set of files: a complete, valid colors.toml and icons.theme, with defaults left to Omarchy's templates. Nothing superfluous.
C.execution_why: It covers the name, the grey-blue low-contrast palette, the muted teal accent, and a background image that strongly fits the 'harbour fog' brief.

D.taste_why: The palette is sound and close to the others, and the solid teal active border is restrained. The wallpaper is very sparse, just a short pier with one teal lamp in a fog band, which risks feeling empty. It also has a visible dark blob artifact in the bottom-left corner.
D.implementation_why: colors.toml is complete. hyprland.lua passes a bare '#6f9e9a' for the active border, whereas Omarchy's configs use rgb()/rgba() forms, so the colour may not parse as intended. The README is harmless filler.
D.execution_why: Every part of the request is present, but the background is thin and slightly flawed, and the border colour format is questionable.

verdict.ranking_why: C pairs a solid palette with the most atmospheric, on-brief harbour wallpaper. A is nearly as good, with an elegant, restrained scene and a reproducible generator. D is competent but its wallpaper is sparse and has a corner artifact, and its border colour format is risky. B's smeared, muddy wallpaper undercuts an otherwise good palette and a nice gradient border.
